guide.step1: Add an account from the Accounts tab (provider Revolut, API Key empty; it is no longer needed, Revolut moved to OAuth).
guide.step2: Here, in Settings: press “Generate certificate”, then “Download the certificate” (a .pem file).
guide.step3: In Revolut Business (business.revolut.com for production, sandbox-business.revolut.com for testing; a separate account, with a normal signup there) go to Settings → APIs → Business API → Add certificate.
guide.step4: Paste the content of the downloaded certificate into the “X509 public key” field. For OAuth redirect URI enter the address where vana-dash runs + /reconciliation/revolut-callback (e.g. https://dash.example.com/reconciliation/revolut-callback on the VPS). Revolut rejects `localhost`: if you test locally without a domain of your own, you can temporarily use a URL from webhook.site to see the authorization code by hand.
guide.step5: Save. Revolut shows you the Client ID. Copy it.
guide.step6: Back in vana-dash: paste the Client ID below, “Save”, then “Open the Revolut consent page”. It takes you to Revolut, where you approve the access.
guide.step7: You are redirected here, to Settings, with the “Authorization code” field already filled in (the code is valid for only ~2 minutes, which is why it is automatic). Check it and press “Connect”.
guide.step8: Done: the status is “Connected”, with automatic refresh from then on (every ~25 min).
guide.title: Guide: setting up Revolut from scratch (sandbox or production)
guide.vpsNote: To remember for the VPS: the variables REVOLUT_API_URL (sandbox-b2b... vs. b2b...) and REVOLUT_REDIRECT_URI in .env must match the environment (sandbox/production) and the real domain exactly. If you change the domain or move to production, update them and redo steps 3-7 (no new certificate is needed; only the redirect URI registered in Revolut has to match).

account.apiKeyHint: Leave empty for Revolut; it is set up separately through OAuth in the Settings tab. Needed only for future providers with a static token.

accounts.title: Bank accounts
accounts.empty: No account connected. Add the Revolut Business account; the OAuth key is set up separately, in the Settings tab.
accounts.deleteBody: The sync stops. The imported transactions and the matches made stay.
accounts.loadFailed: The accounts could not be loaded

transactions.matchCancelled: Match canceled. The invoice is back to unpaid
transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.allMatchedTitle: All transactions are matched with invoices
transactions.allMatchedHint: The filter shows only what is unmatched.
transactions.emptyHint: They show up after the first sync of the bank account.

match.saved: Match saved. The invoice is marked as paid

page.adminOnly: The bank accounts and their keys belong to the company; ask an administrator if you need them here.

revolut.certGenerated: Certificate generated. Download it and upload it in Revolut
revolut.steps: 1. Save the Client ID (from the app registered in Revolut Business Settings → API) · 2. Generate the certificate and upload it there · 3. Open the consent page and paste the code from the redirect.
revolut.setClientIdFirst: Set the Client ID and generate the certificate first, so you can open the consent page.
revolut.noAccount: No Revolut account yet. Add one in the Accounts tab, then come back here to set up OAuth.

extension.title: Vanagreen subscription extension
extension.hint: On a confirmed payment (automatic bank match or a manual “Mark as paid” in Invoices) for a client mapped to a vanagreen tenant, the subscription is extended there. With the switch off, the actions are logged as a dry-run: useful for testing, with no real call to vanagreen.
